title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: Bis(amidinate) lanthanide amide dimers catalyze carboxylation of terminal alkynes with CO2 at ambient pressure through alkyne aminolysis to a metal acetylide, CO2 insertion into the Ln–C bond, and transmetalation with Cs2CO3.
explanation: Ln2 (Ln = La, Nd, Y) clusters convert many terminal alkynes to propiolic acids with broad functional-group tolerance; Nd2 was the most reactive (94% yield). The review also notes that organolanthanides are predisposed to [1,2]-insertion because of electrophilic Ln centers and reactive Ln–X bonds.
scope: Dinuclear organolanthanide amide clusters for C–C bond formation between terminal alkynes and CO2.
conditions: Cs2CO3, 40 °C, 0.1 MPa, 24 h for the Nd2 entry.
caveats: A stoichiometric acid quench is required to release the carboxylic acid from the cesium carboxylate. Related Gd–Cu MOFs operate at 80 °C rather than 40 °C.
